claim: FRANK recurrence should be modeled as a heterogeneous typed loop-of-loops graph rather than one monolithic reasoning loop.
falsifier: single-loop/global-rate architecture matches or exceeds heterogeneous recurrent graph under equal compute and semantics

claim: FRANK-level recurrence and model-internal recurrent-depth are separate design axes; current BASE should compile external recurrence around a conventional model adapter before changing the model architecture.
verification_requirement: executable recurrent FRANK component through current model adapter
falsifier: conventional model adapter cannot preserve required recurrence semantics/performance and recurrent model uniquely resolves the failure

claim: Recurrence does not justify new ClayCode syntax without an executable counterexample; implementation/lowering wins by default during BASE.
verification_requirement: none beyond current program governance; revise only by owner/canonical program change
falsifier: explicit program governance update or executable counterexample admitted under the existing rule

claim: Re-entry should be persisted with episode/event identity plus loop cursor/epoch to make duplicate, delayed, shuffled and provenance-broken controls replayable.
verification_requirement: duplicate/out-of-order and five-arm re-entry Harness tests
falsifier: identity/cursor metadata adds no correctness or causal-specificity value

claim: In a synthetic sparse 10,000-node DAG, 1,000 random source updates affected 30.25 nodes on average (median 2, p95 64.05), yielding a full-sweep/mean-affected operation-count ratio of about 330.6x.
verification_requirement: measure real FRANK affected-set density and scheduler overhead
falsifier: real dependency updates are dense or incremental maintenance removes advantage

claim: On a synthetic mixed slow/fast process, a two-timescale state reduced test MSE from 0.102789 to 0.095984 versus the best one-state EMA (about 6.62% relative improvement).
falsifier: single-timescale state matches multi-timescale under real workloads/equal compute

claim: A synthetic adaptive stopping rule reached MSE 0.005444 at 9.148 mean recurrent steps (p95 19), outperforming fixed-16 MSE 0.008343 while fixed-24/32 achieved lower absolute error at higher compute.
falsifier: adaptive stopping offers no Pareto advantage on target workloads

claim: A toy parent-child effect intersection broker produced zero parent-subset violations in 100,000 random requests while ambient requested effects violated the parent subset in 93.4% of generated cases; this proves only the set-inclusion instrument, not OS/FFI completeness.
falsifier: mediated runtime can exercise an effect outside parent contract

claim: Recurrent safety needs cumulative per-epoch resource/effect budgets because repetition of individually allowed effects can still cause aggregate damage.
falsifier: per-call mediation alone bounds all aggregate protected-state/resource harm in target runtime

claim: Emergence evidence should remain multi-axis: screening/nulls, directed flow, interventionist synergy, macro gain, lesion/rescue, re-entry specificity, implementation transfer, robustness and cost; no single scalar is sufficient.
falsifier: one scalar reliably dominates the multi-axis bundle across confounded/causal/OOD fixtures without Goodhart loss
